Article Title: 'Politicisation of energy flows harmful': Jaishankar calls for diversified supply chains at G20
Article Text:
Jaishankar speaks at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, calling for diversified supply chains and the de-politicisation of energy markets

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday called for reducing political interference in energy markets and diversifying global supply chains, saying disruptions were placing a disproportionate burden on developing countries.Speaking about the message he delivered at G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said the discussions covered geopolitical conflicts, energy and food security, and resilient supply chains.“Look, there are big conflicts today, two major conflicts which are having global ramifications,” ANI quoted him as saying. He added that “there are no military solutions; we have to find a diplomatic pathway.”On energy security, Jaishankar warned against disruptions in fuel distribution and their impact on developing economies. “This distortion of the energy markets, the politicisation of energy flows, this is something which is very harmful,” he said, adding that “the Global South was bearing the brunt of the energy shortages and that something needs to be done.”He also flagged risks to food security, citing disruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea and fertiliser shortages linked to tensions in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea regions.At the meeting's concluding session on supply chains, Jaishankar called for wider diversification of manufacturing and production across countries. “Today we need more diversified supply chains,” he said, advocating “more globalised, you know, more diversified production, more diversified manufacturing.”In a post on X after the session, he said securing supply chains was central to the global economy's well-being and called on the G20 to promote “the right to industrialise” and resist “predatory practices”.“Diversification and de-risking, including in connectivity, is the key to supply chain resilience, threatened by pandemics, conflicts, climate events and mishaps,” he said.Jaishankar also urged the grouping to work towards the “de-politicisation of markets” and prevent the concentration of production and resources in a few geographies.US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who hosted the meeting, also stressed the need to secure critical trade routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb, and strengthen supply chains for critical minerals.On the sidelines, Jaishankar attended a Quad foreign ministers' meeting with Rubio and his Japanese and Australian counterparts. He also met Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov, with discussions covering the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar spoke at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta. He called for the de-politicisation of energy markets and diversified supply chains. He said the Global South was bearing the brunt of energy shortages. He also flagged risks to food security, citing disruptions to grain shipments.

NEW DELHI: A helicopter with six people onboard crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district while travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun. One pilot and five passengers were on board the chopper. The wreckage of a helicopter has been found.The helicopter, reportedly operated by Charlie X-ray Company, was reported missing near Hathi Parvat, prompting authorities to deploy two other choppers to locate it.Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel have been dispatched to the site for relief and rescue operations, officials told PTI."At 14.21hrs, information was received from the SDM Joshimath regarding the crash landing of a helicopter above Chai village in the Joshimath area. In this regard, UCADA officials stated that the location of a Trans Bharat helicopter, which was flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara, is showing near the Army Camp above Chai village," Sub-Inspector Manohar Kanyal, Joshimath Post told news agency ANI.Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami said the aircraft crashed near Chayee village, close to Joshimath, and that a joint rescue operation was underway involving the district administration, disaster management department and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF).“We have received the unfortunate news of a helicopter crash near Chayee village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, disaster management department, and SDRF,” Dhami wrote in a post on X.He added that he was personally monitoring the situation and that instructions had been issued to airlift the seriously injured to advanced medical facilities for treatment.

Article Title: NC faces revolt as 25 MLAs seek removal of ministers, Omar aide
Article Text:
Around 25 NC legislators have sought a cabinet overhaul and the removal of Omar Abdullah’s political adviser, exposing growing discontent within the ruling party

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah faces a growing revolt within National Conference (NC), with around 25 legislators demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers, including the deputy CM, within 15 days and removal of his close aide and political adviser Nasir Aslam Wani.At a meeting at NC MLA Qaiser Jamshaid Lone’s home Friday evening, legislators passed a resolution seeking a cabinet overhaul and wider consultations within the party before portfolios are allocated. Around 18 MLAs attended in person and seven joined online, according to a legislator who was present. NC has 41 MLAs in 90-member assembly and runs a coalition govt with six Congress, six independent and one CPM legislator.“So far there is no next step. The first step was a big step to bring democracy within the party,” the legislator said. The resolution sought removal of all eight ministers and Wani for the “larger good of the party”.NC provincial president for Kashmir Showkat Mir confirmed the meeting but played down its significance, saying it was not directed against the party. He said some senior legislators wanted an appointment with NC president Farooq Abdullah.“Everyone wants to become a minister but the CM can appoint only eight in UT set up,” Mir said, adding that 24 legislators could be accommodated in the cabinet if statehood was restored.Omar, 56, and his father Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi, where the CM celebrated his wedding with journalist Nidhi Razdan. Sharing a photograph on social media, Omar wrote: “A new journey began yesterday.” On July 31, Supreme Court granted Omar a divorce after being informed that he and his estranged wife Payal Abdullah had settled their matrimonial dispute through mediation.The NC turmoil came as party MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi prepared to quit the party and surrender his Lok Sabha seat on Nov 3, accusing Omar and his ministers of betraying the party’s promises on restoration of Article 370 and protection of J&K’s rights.“The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family,” Mehdi wrote on X. He accused NC of seeking votes on promises to restore Article 370 and release prisoners, only to abandon them after assuming office.Mehdi will address people at Budgam on Nov 3, the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, a Congress politician and prominent Shiite cleric assassinated in a terrorist attack on Nov 3, 2000. Mehdi has been among Omar’s sharpest critics, accusing him of abandoning NC’s manifesto.The MLAs’ meeting followed Omar’s cabinet expansion last week, triggering open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in NC after four ministers were inducted, taking the cabinet’s strength to nine, including the CM. He dropped Satish Sharma, leaving only two ministers from Jammu region — deputy CM Surinder Choudhary and Javed Ahmed Rana.BJP has predicted a split in NC and collapse of Omar’s govt. “I am telling you there is unrest against the party brass. They are looking for an alternative. Govt will not remain and the party will not remain,” leader of opposition Sunil Sharma said. He described Omar as a “prince, who doesn’t want to listen to any legislator”.
Article Summary: Around 25 NC legislators have sought a cabinet overhaul and the removal of Omar Abdullah’s political adviser, exposing growing discontent within the ruling party. The resolution sought removal of all eight ministers and Wani for the ‘larger good of the party’

Article Title: ‘Water ingress’ incident on Navy vessel, no casualties reported
Article Text:
Water entered INS Kesari while it was berthed at Visakhapatnam’s Naval Dockyard, with the Navy reporting no casualties and dewatering efforts underway

NEW DELHI: The Indian Navy on Saturday confirmed an incident of “water ingress” (flooding) on one of its ships while the vessel was berthed at the Naval Dockyard in Visakhapatnam . The incident was reported on INS Kesari, a Shardul-class tank landing ship.The Navy, in an official statement, said that “no casualties have been reported”. Efforts to pump out the water are underway, it added.INS Kesari, which was commissioned on April 5, 2008, has a 5,650-tonne displacement.Deployed in May 2020 for Mission Sagar, INS Kesari had delivered Covid-19 relief material, medical assistance and food items to nations in the southern Indian Ocean, such as Maldives, Mauritius, Madagascar, Comoros and Seychelles.
Article Summary: Water entered INS Kesari while it was berthed at Visakhapatnam’s Naval Dockyard. The Navy, in an official statement, said that “no casualties have been reported’ Efforts to pump out the water are underway, it added.

Article Title: 'Will deal with Modi, Shah': Rahul Gandhi explains why CEC Gyanesh Kumar is his first target
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability.

'We are not going to let you escape'

INDIA bloc holds 'public impeachment' of CEC

BJP calls it 'mockery' of democracy

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah may be at the top of the political chain of command, but Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that the opposition's first target is Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Explaining why the INDIA bloc has upped its attack on the election chief, the Congress leader accused him of acting as an instrument of the ruling establishment and warned that those allegedly involved in undermining democratic institutions would be held accountable."Mr Modi and Mr Shah might be on top. We will deal with them, but you are their instruments, and so you are our first target," Rahul Gandhi said on Saturday at the INDIA bloc event in Delhi, where opposition leaders held a symbolic public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability."So if Mr Gyanesh Kumar thinks, or the five or seven people below him think, that immunity will save them, I would kindly suggest to them, with love and affection, to take a look at what is going on in the country. Please understand the mood of the people outside.You will see tomorrow itself," he said.Rahul Gandhi was referring to the opposition's planned march and public rally in Delhi on Sunday, which he described as an opportunity for a united opposition to demonstrate public anger over alleged electoral irregularities."A united opposition is going to show you exactly what the mood of the people of this country is," he said.Rahul Gandhi said the opposition's action against CEC was not an isolated protest against one constitutional functionary but part of a larger fight over what he alleged was the misuse of democratic institutions."You can continue to rig the elections. You can continue to control and allow the misuse of the CBI, the ED, and every single institution of this country. But we guarantee you that this is a temporary phenomenon," he said.The Congress leader insisted that Gyanesh Kumar was only one among several people the opposition held responsible for what it described as an assault on the country's democratic institutions."We are not going to let you escape. I also want to address the people who have carried out this assault on the Union of India. Gyanesh Kumar is just one element; there are many others. We know who they are, and we understand deeply who they are," Rahul Gandhi said."This is a warning to you: things are shifting. Please hear this warning and realise that this is a new political weapon sitting in the garden, and this weapon is going to hurt you very badly if you continue down your path," he said."I am saying this with love and affection; we are not nasty or evil people, but we will protect the Constitution and the voice of our people."Rahul Gandhi also backed the demand for legal action against the CEC, saying Gyanesh Kumar should not only face impeachment but also be tried in court for treason."I fully support the motion that Mr Gyanesh Kumar should not only be impeached but should also be tried in a court of law for treason so that justice can be served," he said.Rahul Gandhi's remarks came at an unprecedented INDIA bloc event in which opposition MPs and leaders, along with civil society representatives, passed a resolution seeking Gyanesh Kumar's impeachment and accusing him of facilitating the deletion of voters' names to influence election outcomes.The symbolic proceedings were held at the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the meeting, which was organised in a setting resembling parliamentary proceedings.The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition MPs and civil society members. It was adopted unanimously by a show of hands.Around 250 opposition MPs, civil society representatives and mediapersons attended the event. Some people who alleged that their names had been wrongly deleted from electoral rolls were also present.Rahul Gandhi acknowledged that holding what resembled parliamentary proceedings outside Parliament might appear unusual, but said the opposition had been left with little choice."I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history," he said, adding that the gathering of opposition leaders and civil society members in a garden might appear absurd."But we had no other option, as every single institution is closed to us," he said.The stage was designed to resemble the old Lok Sabha chamber, with a wooden-panelled backdrop and seats arranged in a semi-circular formation.Kharge, who moved the motion, alleged that the right to vote was under threat because the Election Commission was functioning at the behest of PM Modi and Shah. He accused the poll panel of failing to act independently and raised concerns over alleged electoral manipulation.The BJP hit back at the opposition's symbolic proceedings, accusing the INDIA bloc of making a mockery of Parliament and democratic institutions.BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, alleging that the Congress was repeatedly attempting to launch its leader politically without success."Go ahead and hold your mock Parliament or take out your marches; the world has already understood that Rahul Gandhi simply lacks the fuel. This 'satellite' is never going to launch," Patra said.He added that the opposition could have Gandhi as a "mock Prime Minister for life".
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi warns the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability. Opposition leaders hold symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Gandhi backs demand for legal action against CEC, saying he should also be tried in court for treason.

Article Title: 'India not a banana republic': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc rally
Article Text:
BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over INDIA bloc rally, alleges bid to create unrest

BJP accuses Opposition of disrupting peace and business

INDIA bloc leaders allege voter irregularities, restrictions on rally supporters

Heavy security arrangements across Delhi

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, accusing the opposition of using the banner of democracy to create unrest, damage the economy and destabilise an elected government.Reacting to the 'Chalo Delhi' mobilisation, Nadda said the rally was a “calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy—in the name of democracy”. He described it as a “foolish, orchestrated drama” by parties that had been defeated and rejected by voters.Addressing Rahul Gandhi directly, the Union minister outlined what he called the Congress leader's model of politics, alleging that it involved spreading misinformation, provoking street protests, harming the economy and seeking to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers.“The first stage is spreading lies and rumours; the second is inciting anarchy and chaos on the streets; the third is damaging the nation’s economy; and the fourth is attempting to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers,” Nadda said.He also alleged that the November 1 rally had four specific objectives: hurting the sentiments of the Sikh community, triggering violence in Delhi to bring down a democratically elected government, affecting the earnings of traders during the festive season and damaging India's reputation.Nadda's remarks came amid the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: this is India—not some 'banana republic' where you can incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for 'regime change' whenever you please. Stop dreaming, Rahul Gandhi. India is the world’s oldest and most robust democracy. November 1st stands as the most infamous and darkest stain in India’s democratic history. On this very day, goons nurtured by the Congress party massacred our innocent Sikh brethren. Thousands of Sikh families were rendered homeless overnight, and thousands of women were widowed. The nation has not forgotten; even today, the 'Widow Colony' in Delhi bears witness to that horrific and bloody chapter of Congress history. To this day, the Gandhi family has not offered a sincere apology to the Sikh community for that grave sin. Observe the insensitivity of the Congress and the petty mindset of Rahul Gandhi. On this dark day—a day when the nation ought to be remembering its martyrs and victims—Rahul Gandhi stands at Ramlila Maidan, seeking only to further his own political agenda ...", Nadda added.The rally has also drawn criticism from the BJP over its timing, with the ruling party accusing Congress of holding a political event on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.BJP is holding a separate march in West Delhi under the banner of remembering the victims of the 1984 violence.The march is scheduled to proceed from Hari Nagar Bus Depot to Tilak Nagar Metro Station, with Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, Delhi BJP president and other party leaders expected to participate.Meanwhile, the BJP and its Mahayuti allies held a 'Lokshahi Bachao, Anarajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) padyatra in Mumbai on Sunday.Maharashtra BJP president Ravindra Chavan accused the Congress of spreading what he described as false narratives about constitutional institutions, including the judiciary and Parliament.“At a time when the entire nation is witnessing a phase of development-oriented governance under the leadership of PM Modi, the opposition Congress party is, without any valid reason, attempting to create confusion among the public by propagating false narratives about our established institutions,” Chavan said.Shiv Sena MP Naresh Mhaske also criticised Rahul Gandhi and his associates, alleging that their activities were against the Constitution.BJP has also launched a nationwide 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign to counter opposition allegations relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Party workers are expected to reach villages and households to present the BJP's position on the electoral process.The opposition alliance, meanwhile, has maintained that its mobilisation is aimed at protecting democratic rights and raising concerns over alleged deletions of legitimate voters from electoral rolls.Himachal Pradesh deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri alleged that buses carrying supporters from his state were being stopped at different points on their way to Delhi.He claimed that some vehicles were intercepted over pollution norms and others over taxation issues, despite the buses being BS-VI-compliant.“We had already instructed everyone that such obstructions might occur, and if stopped, they should simply continue on foot to reach Himachal Bhawan,” Agnihotri said, adding that the supporters were prepared to walk to Ramlila Maidan.Himachal Pradesh minister Vikramaditya Singh called for accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and claimed that the number of votes involved in the alleged irregularities had risen from 13 crore to around 16 crore.“I am confident that, in the near future, the CEC Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign, and a new revolution will sweep across the entire country,” Singh said.Uttarakhand leader of opposition Yashpal Arya described the rally as a “battle for justice” to protect democracy and the Constitution. Congress leader Kunwar Danish Ali also called the mobilisation historic and accused the government of targeting students, young people and farmers.The INDIA bloc has demanded the replacement of electronic voting machines with paper ballots and the immediate resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people in Delhi and neighbouring states to join the march, either from Connaught Place or directly at Ramlila Maidan.Security has been tightened across the national capital in view of the two political events. Nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel, including Delhi Police, Central Armed Police Forces, the CRPF and Rapid Action Force, have been deployed across Central and New Delhi, ANI reported.More than 4,000 personnel have been stationed around Ramlila Maidan, along the route from Minto Bridge and in surrounding areas. Barricades have also been placed around Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar, Bhagwan Das Road and areas near the Supreme Court and the Election Commission's office.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita has been imposed in sensitive areas to prevent large unauthorised gatherings. Security agencies are also using CCTV cameras, AI-enabled facial recognition systems and drones to monitor crowd movement.At the Delhi-Gurugram border, Border Security Force personnel have been deployed alongside police units to monitor entry points into the capital. Authorities have installed barricades on major routes connecting the two cities and are checking suspicious vehicles.
Article Summary: Union minister JP Nadda launches sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. He accuses the opposition of using the banner of democracy to create unrest, damage the economy and destabilise an elected government.

Article Title: 'No military solutions': EAM Jaishankar reveals PM Modi-Putin talks on Ukraine conflict in Delhi, Bishkek
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi with Russian President Vladimir Putin

India focuses on civilian shipping, grain exports and energy security

Jaishankar calls for diplomatic solutions to global conflicts

Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has said Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed the Ukraine conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin in New Delhi and earlier in Bishkek, as India continues diplomatic engagement with Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on measures to protect civilian shipping, restore grain exports and safeguard energy infrastructure.Speaking exclusively to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta on Saturday, Jaishankar said India had held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on three key aspects of the conflict."Prime Minister himself had a discussion with President Putin in Delhi and before that in Bishkek," he said, referring to India's diplomatic engagement.Jaishankar said he had also discussed the conflict with Russian and Ukrainian officials, including during visits to Moscow and Kyiv, and in talks with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov."We have also been coordinating this with the Americans because they have their own peace mediation initiative. So Secretary Rubio knows properly what is going on here," he said.Explaining the three areas under discussion, Jaishankar said India was first seeking to ensure that civilian vessels and seafarers were not targeted in the conflict.The second priority was to restore grain exports from Russia and Ukraine, both major suppliers to international markets.He said shipments through the Black Sea had fallen sharply because of the conflict."One not to attack civilian shipping and seafarers. The second is to find a way by which the grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine. Then these are two major exporters of grains for the global markets. Find a way of restoring that flow because that flow has cut down very sharply in the Black Sea," he said.The third area concerned energy infrastructure and shipments. Jaishankar said this was the most complicated issue because the concerns differed among the parties involved."Non-attack on energy is probably the most complicated piece because it means different things to the different players," he said, referring to refineries, electricity grids and ships carrying fuel.He added that India was trying to bring the parties together to address these concerns but could not publicly disclose the current status of the discussions.At the G20 meeting, the external affairs minister reiterated India's position that major international conflicts required diplomatic engagement rather than military escalation."Look, there are big conflicts today, two major conflicts which are having global ramifications," he said, adding that "there are no military solutions; we have to find a diplomatic pathway."Jaishankar also flagged the impact of disruptions in energy markets and fuel distribution on developing economies."This distortion of the energy markets, the politicisation of energy flows, this is something which is very harmful," he said, adding that the Global South was bearing the brunt of energy shortages.He also raised concerns over disruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea and fertiliser shortages linked to tensions along the Persian Gulf and Red Sea corridors.On supply chain resilience, which was the focus of the G20 meeting's concluding plenary session, Jaishankar called for greater diversification of global production and manufacturing networks."Today we need more diversified supply chains," he said, advocating "more globalised, you know, more diversified production, more diversified manufacturing."In a post on X after the session, he said securing resilient supply chains was central to the well-being of the global economy. He also called for promoting the "right to industrialise", resisting "predatory practices" and pursuing the "de-politicisation of markets".On the sidelines of the G20 meeting, Jaishankar held separate discussions with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts on the Ukraine conflict, West Asia, bilateral ties and multilateral issues.After meeting Lavrov, Jaishankar said the two sides had discussed the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues.He also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, with discussions focusing on the Ukraine conflict, India-European Union ties and the G20."My meeting with DPM & FM Radosław Sikorski @sikorskiradek of Poland focused on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20," Jaishankar said.Poland is participating in this year's G20 meetings as a full participant following an invitation from the United States. It has also expressed interest in securing permanent membership of the grouping.Jaishankar separately met South Korean foreign minister Cho Hyun to review bilateral cooperation and discuss G20-related and other multilateral issues."Appreciated the stocktaking with @FMChoHyun of the Republic of Korea of our bilateral cooperation, as also the discussion on G20 and multilateral issues," he said.Earlier on Saturday, Jaishankar also participated in the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian foreign minister Penny Wong.The US is holding the G20 presidency this year. After two days of discussions, Jaishankar and other foreign ministers attended a college football game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.
Article Summary: India continues diplomatic engagement with Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on measures to protect civilian shipping, restore grain exports and safeguard energy infrastructure. External affairs minister reiterated India's position that major international conflicts required diplomatic engagement rather than military escalation. Jaishankar held separate discussions with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts on the Ukraine conflict.

Article Title: 'Remarkable valour': PM Modi pays tribute to Haryana's heritage on foundation day
Article Text:
Celebrating its 60th Foundation Day on November 1, Haryana showcased its rich heritage and remarkable achievements. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Amit Shah, Rahul Gandhi extend greetings

Haryana marks six decades of statehood

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended greetings to the people of Haryana as the state marked 60 years since its formation, praising its rich cultural heritage, sporting achievements and contributions to the country's growth.In a message posted on X, PM Modi highlighted Haryana's glorious history, courage and vibrant rural traditions, noting that its folk culture has played an important role in enriching India's cultural identity."Heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all my family members of the state on Haryana Day! Our state, adorned with a glorious history, remarkable valor, and a rich culture, is the pride of the nation. The folk traditions and vibrant rural culture here have always enriched the nation's cultural heritage," the Prime Minister wrote.PM Modi also acknowledged the contributions of Haryana's athletes and farmers, saying they have brought recognition to the country on international platforms and strengthened its food security."The people of Haryana have proven their talent and determination from agriculture, sports, and defence services to industry, education, and startups through their hard work and dedication.The athletes here are enhancing the honour of the tricolour, while the food providers are strengthening the country's food security. I wish that this special occasion brings prosperity into the lives of all the people here," he added.Union home minister Amit Shah also conveyed his wishes to Haryana's residents, describing the state as a land of courage, hard work and prosperity. In his message on X, he highlighted its contributions to national security, sports, agriculture and animal husbandry."Heartfelt greetings to all the residents of the state on the Foundation Day of Haryana, the land of valor, labour, and prosperity. Be it defending the nation on the borders, enhancing the honour of the tricolour on the sports fields, or setting new benchmarks in agriculture and animal husbandry, Haryana's contribution in every field is unparalleled," Amit Shah wrote.He further praised the state's soldiers, sportspersons and farmers for their role in strengthening India's reputation and economic progress, expressing hope that Haryana would continue to advance.Leader of the opposition in the lok sabha Rahul Gandhi also extended greetings to people across several states and union territories celebrating their foundation days on November 1.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi highlighted the country's diverse cultural traditions, languages and regional identities, saying they have shaped India's national character. He wished the regions continued prosperity and progress while contributing to a united nation.The Congress party also issued greetings to residents of Haryana and other states and Union territories marking their formation anniversaries. It called for continued progress, unity and commitment to constitutional values.At the state level, chief minister Nayab Singh Saini attended the foundation day celebrations in Chandigarh, marking six decades since Haryana became a separate state on November 1, 1966.Recalling the state's journey, Saini acknowledged the contributions of those who had campaigned for its formation and worked towards its development."We express our gratitude to all the great personalities who struggled for the formation of Haryana and worked hard for the construction of modern Haryana. On this day in 1966, when it became a separate state, it was very backward. Our farmer benefactors, hardworking labourers, diligent industrialists and traders, and valiant sportspersons all made a significant contribution in transforming that backward region into a modern, developed Haryana," the chief minister said.Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Punjab and Tamil Nadu observe their state formation day on November 1. Several union territories, including Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep, also mark their foundation day on the occasion.
Article Summary: Haryana marks six decades of statehood on November 1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people of Haryana. He praised its rich cultural heritage, sporting achievements and contributions to the country's growth. Union home minister Amit Shah also conveyed his wishes to the state's residents.

Article Title: Sardar Patel had said if Pandit Nehru had not intervened, he would have integrated Kashmir as easily as Hyderabad: Rajnath Singh
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh pays tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary, recalling his role in Hyderabad's integration and saying Patel could have integrated Kashmir as easily had Nehru not intervened.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Paying rich tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary, defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday recalled how the ‘Iron Man of India’ firmly dealt with the Nizam and Razakars, who sought to challenge India’s sovereignty and “laid the foundation of a strong and united India”. On the issue of Kashmir, Rajnath said, “Sardar Patel himself had said that if Pandit Nehru had not intervened, he would have integrated Kashmir as easily as Hyderabad.”Addressing a gathering, the defence minister said, “Sardar Patel was the architect of India’s political and territorial unity, whose extraordinary leadership, courage and unwavering commitment to national interest laid the foundation of a strong and united India”.He further said, “In democracy, govts are formed by winning the trust of the people and on the basis of public opinion, not through violence and anarchy. The path to change of power is elections, not coups. Those who challenge the unity and integrity of India should not forget the history of Sardar Patel.” “Those who dream of weakening India or creating disorder must remember that the land which gave birth to Sardar Patel has also given birth to Narendra Modi,” the minister said.He also criticised Congress and its allies for their use of the term 'regime change'. He emphasised that ‘regime change’ essentially implies a coup, violence, anarchy and civil war.Rajnath said that Sardar Patel firmly believed that India should never seek what does not belong to it, but should never give up what rightfully belongs to it, under any circumstances. He said that India continues to move forward guided by this very principle. “India does not seek to occupy anyone else's territory, nor does it initiate conflict. However, it remains resolute in securing what rightfully belongs to it and safeguarding its national interests. ”He further asserted that whether it is avenging terrorist attacks or reclaiming Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK), India remains firmly committed to defending its rights and sovereignty.Recalling the events surrounding the Congress presidential election of 1946, the minister said that despite overwhelming support from provincial Congress committees, Sardar Patel withdrew his candidature in deference to Mahatma Gandhi's wishes. “For Sardar Patel, the country was always bigger than the chair. Duty was more important than position, and national interest was greater than personal ambition. ”The defence minister expressed concern over what he described as the historical neglect of Sardar Patel’s contributions and recalled that Patel was conferred the Bharat Ratna only in 1991, nearly four decades after his demise. He also referred to the contrast between the celebrations of Jawaharlal Nehru's birth centenary in 1989 and the relatively subdued observance of Sardar Patel's birth centenary in 1975. He credited PM Modi with restoring national recognition to Patel's legacy through the Statue of Unity, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, Run for Unity and Ekta March. “Sardar Patel was a great leader in his own right. Honouring him has not made him any greater; rather, it has brought greater honour to India.”Highlighting Sardar Patel's emphasis on military modernisation and indigenous production of weapons and ammunition, Rajnath said that India's growing defence manufacturing capabilities reflect the spirit of self-reliance that Patel advocated. He said that Sardar Patel's legacy extends far beyond the integration of princely states. It is reflected in India's strong administrative institutions, national security, social harmony and commitment to national interest. He said that the vision of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat' and the mission of building a Viksit Bharat are inspired by the ideals that Sardar Patel upheld throughout his life.“India's greatest strength lies in its unity. We must never allow internal differences to weaken our national resolve. Preserving India's unity and integrity is the responsibility of every citizen,” he said.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh pays tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary. He recalled his role in Hyderabad's integration and said Patel could have integrated Kashmir as easily had Nehru not intervened. He also criticised Congress and its allies for their use of the term'regime change'

NEW DELHI: At its two-day national meet, the Jamiat Ulama-i- Hind (JUH)’s governing council passed resolutions calling for the establishment of special fast track courts to deal with hate crimes and cited Census data and its own research to reject the narrative that Muslims are seeking to alter the country’s demographic balance through “demographic jihad” and illegal infiltration.According to a statement issued by the JUH faction led by Maulana Mahmood Madani, the Jamiat president said, “Those conspiring to turn Muslims into outsiders and second-class citizens in their own country are, in fact, enemies of the nation”.He was addressing the event held in Nuh, Mewat.Madani observed that hate speech could no longer be dismissed as a temporary instrument of electoral politics. NEW DELHI: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) is open to debates on national issues but people must remain vigilant to ensure that forces opposed to the country's interests do not misuse public protests, senior Sangh leader Sunil Ambekar said on Saturday.Ambekar, the RSS's Akhil Bharatiya Prachar Pramukh, said the organisation had been engaged in debates on its views on Hindutva, nationalism and other issues for more than 100 years.He added that RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and other functionaries were willing to engage in dialogue on these subjects.He was speaking to the media ahead of the RSS's annual meeting, scheduled to begin in Indore on November 2.Asked whether the RSS was late in reaching out to younger people, particularly after recent Gen Z protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, Ambekar said it was wrong to assume that the organisation automatically supported or opposed those raising questions about national issues."If someone in the country raises their voice on an issue, why do you consider the Sangh to be either for or against it? That is a wrong way of thinking. If someone raises a question concerning the country, that is fine. They have the right to do so," he said.Referring to Bhagwat's address at the RSS's Vijayadashami celebrations in Nagpur, Ambekar said protests should serve the country's interests and contribute to its progress.“As the Sarsanghchalak (Mohan Bhagwat) also said in his address at the (RSS) Vijayadashami celebrations in Nagpur, everyone must ensure that any protests taking place in the country are in the country's interest and aimed at taking it forward. Therefore, everyone must remain vigilant to ensure that forces opposed to the country's interests do not infiltrate protests and misuse them.”Ambekar said the RSS remained attentive to the issue and would continue to engage with it. Ambekar said the RSS did not oppose emerging mass communication platforms or new technologies, but stressed the need to use them responsibly."The Sangh does not oppose any mass communication medium or its new technology, but as human beings, we certainly need to think about how we use these platforms. The Sangh will continue to work towards creating awareness in society on this issue," he said.He also said youth participation in RSS activities was growing. Around two lakh people attended the organisation's introductory training camps last year, while more than 13,000 new shakhas were started over the past year, he said.On the University Grants Commission's (UGC) controversial equity regulations, Ambekar said the RSS had already described the circular as "imbalanced".He said the government and the UGC had taken note of the concerns raised and that the court had stayed the regulations. The matter is currently before the court, he added."Our position is that whatever happens next on this issue should be balanced, and the government must ensure this," Ambekar said.He also cautioned against allowing a single circular to disrupt social harmony, stressing the need for unity.The University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, notified in January, require higher education institutions to set up equity committees to examine complaints of discrimination and promote equality.The committees are required to include members from the Other Backward Classes (OBC), Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST), as well as persons with disabilities and women.
Article Summary: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) is open to debates on national issues. But people must remain vigilant to ensure that forces opposed to the country's interests do not misuse public protests, senior Sangh leader Sunil Ambekar says.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri on Saturday said the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was a profound tragedy but stressed that it could not justify the violence subsequently inflicted on the Sikh community during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.Ahead of the 42nd anniversary of the riots on November 1, Puri said, "The assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, regardless of one’s perspective, was a profound tragedy.
