Article Title: Philadelphia professor arrested for blocking delivery robots, says she would do it again because she believes she has more rights than a robot
Article Text:
Retired professor has been arrested for blocking a delivery robot in Philadelphia.

Why delivery robots have legal protection

A 78-year-old retired professor in Philadelphia has vowed to continue protesting delivery robots after she was arrested for repeatedly standing in their way, arguing that her actions were an exercise of free speech and a protest against technology taking over public spaces.Carolyn Marvin, a retired communications professor at the University of Pennsylvania, said blocking autonomous delivery robots had become a habit since the small, wheeled machines began operating on Philadelphia’s streets and sidewalks.October 14 was not the first time Marvin had placed herself in front of one of the robots. She would stop them for a few minutes as they travelled along the sidewalk carrying food orders.“I was under the impression that I had more rights than the robot did,” Marvin said to CNN in an inerview.The October 14 incident ended with her arrest. Marvin said she had been returning home after getting a flu shot when she encountered a delivery robot. She had a jar of enchilada sauce in one hand and chicken biryani takeout in the other when she stood in front of the machine, as she had done on previous occasions.The incident took place in a busy part of the city, and a larger-than-usual crowd gathered.Some people supported her, while others criticized her. Marvin suspects someone in the crowd eventually called the police.Officers handcuffed her, put her in a police vehicle and issued her a citation for disorderly conduct.Philadelphia police said they had responded to a report of “criminal mischief involving a delivery robot”. When officers arrived, they found a woman “who was refusing to allow a delivery robot to pass”, according to an email from the police department. Officers issued multiple commands asking her to move, but she refused to comply.Marvin said she never expected to be arrested because she believed she was not obstructing another person.“I wasn’t impeding any persons. I was impeding a machine,” she said.She described her actions as a symbolic protest against the problems associated with delivery robots, including the displacement of low-income delivery workers, the physical risks the machines could pose to people using sidewalks and privacy concerns arising from their built-in cameras.“I also think that I have a First Amendment right to protest the abuses of corporations in public space, in the same public space that the robots are occupying,” she said.Marvin said she had previously taken part in protests supporting civil rights and abortion rights, supporting Black Lives Matter and opposing the Gulf and Vietnam wars. She sees her campaign against delivery robots as an extension of the same impulse to make the government hear public concerns.She said blocking the machines had also led to conversations with passersby who wanted to know what she was doing. Most were supportive or curious.Marvin said her protest had a limited impact on customers, with an office worker’s lunch potentially delayed by around 15 minutes at most. She added that she did not have unlimited time to spend blocking robots and would do so for 10 or 15 minutes when it was “convenient and possible”.A friend summed up her arrest by telling her: “Well, you got a disorderly conduct charge for impeding capitalism.”Following her arrest, Marvin learnt more about the legal framework governing autonomous delivery devices in Pennsylvania.In 2020, the state legislature passed a law classifying autonomous delivery robots, described in the legislation as “personal delivery devices”, as pedestrians rather than vehicles.The legislation was largely opposed by Democrats, labour unions and accessibility advocates, who argued that allowing delivery robots could threaten jobs and put children and pedestrians at risk. Republicans supported the measure, describing it as an exciting technological development.The law requires vehicles to yield to delivery robots at crosswalks, just as they would to pedestrians, John Mattiacci, a Philadelphia personal injury attorney told CNN.However, the machines are also required to give way to people and cyclists in pedestrian areas.“Personal delivery devices must yield to other pedestrians and pedalcyclists in a pedestrian area,” Mattiacci said.Uber Eats introduced robot deliveries in Philadelphia in March, making it the fourth city where the company offered the service. However, not everyone has welcomed the robots. Videos recorded in Philadelphia and other cities have shown people sitting on the machines, kicking them and causing damage.Marvin sees the growing presence of delivery robots as part of a wider trend in which technology and machines are increasingly occupying everyday spaces.“There’s a way in which we’ve surrendered the streets to cars long ago, and I don’t think we should surrender the sidewalks to machines,” she said.“Machines in general encroach on our lives,” she added. “Public space is the most visible place where they’re encroaching on our lives, but they’re going right up the ladder, and lots of people are interested in making that happen.”She said robots were a visible symbol of the wider spread of technology, including artificial intelligence and social media algorithms that influence the images and narratives people consume.Her protest, she said, helps make the issue visible and presents it in a way that might otherwise go unnoticed.Asked whether she planned to resume blocking delivery robots after her arrest, Marvin had a brief answer: “Oh yeah.”This time, however, she said she would keep an eye out for the police.
Article Summary: Carolyn Marvin, 78, was arrested for blocking a delivery robot in Philadelphia. She said her actions were an exercise of free speech and a protest against technology taking over public spaces. Marvin said she never expected to be arrested because she believed she was not obstructing another person.

Article Title: why is Gen Z taking to the streets across Germany
Article Text:
Halloween masks, Gen Z protest: Demonstrators take to streets in Germany

Halloween meets protest as Gen Z rallies in Germany

Police blame extremist groups for violence

'Gen Z Takes Care of It'

What are Germany's Gen Z protesters demanding?

Turnout falls short of organisers' expectations

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the protests organized by GenZ regelt! in Germany? Yes, I support their demands. No, I disagree with their approach. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Questions over who is leading the movement

Thousands of young people took to the streets across Germany on Saturday to protest against rising living costs, cuts in education spending and plans to strengthen the country's military, but demonstrations in several cities turned violent in the evening, with rioters looting shops and clashing with police.The protests, organised by the youth campaign group "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z takes charge), were held in 34 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The movement drew inspiration from youth-led demonstrations in other European countries, particularly France and Italy, where young people have been demanding greater attention to their concerns.While the demonstrations remained largely peaceful during the day, violence broke out in major cities including Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg as some groups refused to disperse.According to AFP, masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt, while police used water cannons and pepper spray against demonstrators who threw stones, fireworks and petrol bombs at security personnel and emergency workers.Police described the situation in Frankfurt as involving "violent riots" and said several shops had their windows smashed. Molotov cocktails were also thrown at emergency personnel, according to a police statement cited by AFP.A gun store was among the establishments targeted, with its windows smashed. Police arrested a suspect and seized two weapons. A trainer shop and a perfume store were also reportedly looted, according to German daily Bild.A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed as police attempted to bring the situation under control. Police vans and riot officers prevented people from entering the area, while a helicopter hovered overhead.At least one police officer was injured in Frankfurt and received medical treatment. Police also reported injuries to officers in other cities.Authorities said the protests had been infiltrated by extremist groups, raising concerns about the possibility of violence spreading during demonstrations.Roman Poseck, interior minister of the German state of Hesse, said around 100 identified left-wing extremists had joined the protest in Frankfurt."It is shameful how this event here in Frankfurt has ended," Poseck said.Police also deployed water cannons in Hamburg and Cologne after demonstrators allegedly targeted emergency service personnel with fireworks, stones and bottles.In Berlin, a separate evening protest, which was not organised by the GenZ regelt! movement, saw demonstrators throw eggs and bottles at police. A police officer in Bonn also suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group.According to Reuters, Germany's federal interior ministry had warned ahead of the demonstrations that parts of the country's far-left extremist scene and groups linked to foreign extremist movements were trying to mobilise support.Hesse's interior minister had also cautioned against the possibility of violence similar to the unrest witnessed in France."We all have those images from France in our minds - looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers," Poseck told Reuters."France must not be held up as a model in this regard."Some businesses in German cities had boarded up their windows and planned to close early ahead of the demonstrations. Concerns were particularly high along Berlin's luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard.The GenZ regelt! movement, however, distanced itself from violence and said extremist groups had no place in its demonstrations."Extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism and hate speech have no place with us - no matter from which side," the group said.The demonstrations were driven by concerns over the rising cost of living, the condition of schools and universities, government spending cuts and increased military expenditure.The movement also opposes compulsory military service and has called for greater investment in education and public services.Young people in Germany have expressed concerns about the government's plans to increase troop numbers through a new voluntary military service model, fearing that it could eventually lead to the return of compulsory conscription.The protests come at a time when Europe's largest economy is struggling to revive growth and facing increasing pressure on its pension system and public services.Germany is also dealing with demographic challenges as large sections of the baby boomer generation approach retirement, reducing the size of its working-age population and putting additional pressure on younger generations.For many protesters, the issue is not limited to military policy or education spending but also concerns the government's priorities and the financial burden being placed on young people."The government has offered no response to our concerns other than to continue making cuts and piling further burdens upon us," Steve, an 18-year-old scheduled to address a rally in Munich, told Reuters.Addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz, he said the protesters would continue exercising their right to assemble until their concerns were addressed.In Berlin, Technical University student Sean Baker told Reuters that the poor condition of university buildings was among the reasons he planned to join the demonstration."When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building," he said. "Yet this is where we're expected to study on a regular basis."The demonstrations were planned across 34 German cities, with organisers initially expecting around 182,000 participants.However, official figures available on Saturday afternoon indicated that turnout was significantly lower than anticipated.Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported around 6,000 participants, compared with approximately 36,000 recorded on the organisers' website, Reuters reported.The movement's organisers later said around 120,000 people had participated nationwide, below their initial estimate of about 180,000, AFP reported.The demonstrations also coincided with Halloween celebrations, with some participants dressed in costumes ranging from dinosaurs to Batman. Protesters carried placards with slogans such as "Time for resistance" and "Merz must go", targeting the policies of the conservative chancellor.In Berlin, a 20-year-old student identified only as Milla told AFP that she wanted to show solidarity with similar demonstrations taking place across Europe."I've been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step," she said.Despite its youth-focused agenda, questions have emerged over whether GenZ regelt! is genuinely a student-led movement, given the involvement of a broad mix of political and civil society groups.Germany's national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has distanced itself from the campaign and announced plans to organise a separate day of protests on November 20."We are distancing ourselves from 'GenZ regelt' but not from the students themselves, who have legitimate concerns," BSK Secretary-General Amy Kirchhoff said on Thursday, according to Reuters.The distinction highlights a wider debate over who represents Germany's younger generation and how their concerns should be raised.The protests are part of a wider wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism played a role in challenging the country's political leadership, while demonstrations in France have witnessed clashes, looting and widespread unrest.The developments have prompted German authorities to remain cautious about the possibility of similar violence spreading to the country.
Article Summary: Thousands of young people took to the streets across Germany on Saturday to protest against rising living costs, cuts in education spending and plans to strengthen the country's military. The protests were organised by the youth campaign group "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z takes charge) The movement drew inspiration from youth-led demonstrations in other European countries, particularly France and Italy, where young people have been demanding greater attention to their concerns.

Article Title: ‘Attempted murder’: Molotov cocktail hits Paris police officer as France protests turn violent
Article Text:
A police officer was struck by a Molotov cocktail in Paris during violent protests over living costs, with 565 arrested across France

Protests spread across Europe

Halloween masks, Gen Z protest: Demonstrators take to streets in Germany

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the recent protests in Paris? Justified Unjustified Mixed feelings Indifferent 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A police officer was struck by a Molotov cocktail during clashes in Paris on Saturday, as demonstrations over rising living costs and deteriorating public services turned violent in several French cities.The interior ministry said 565 people had been arrested across France. Four police officers and one gendarme were injured in Paris, with three officers suffering burns from Molotov cocktails. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said around 150 planned demonstrations had passed off peacefully but condemned what he described as an “extraordinary” level of violence by some groups as the rallies ended.An estimated 320,000 people took part in demonstrations across the country, down from 410,000 the previous weekend, according to the interior ministry. Around 70,000 marched in Paris, where protesters set off from Porte de Bagnolet and headed towards Porte de Charenton, largely avoiding the city centre.The march was mostly peaceful until it reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to prise up paving stones and throw them at police, while at least one incendiary device was hurled at security forces, AFP journalists reported.Police responded with tear gas and baton charges. The Paris police prefecture said several hundred rioters had attacked officers with projectiles.The violence came despite a major security deployment. Nuñez had announced that 70,000 police officers and gendarmes, including elite units, would be deployed across the country, warning that Saturday was expected to be a high-risk day. He described the attack on the police officer with a Molotov cocktail as an “attempted murder”.The demonstrations brought together school students, trade unions and Yellow Vest protesters, united by anger over the cost of living, widening inequalities and the state of public services under French president Emmanuel Macron’s government. Some protesters wore Halloween costumes, carrying placards and slogans reflecting their anger.In Lyon, clashes broke out after protesters threw projectiles at police, who responded with tear gas. In Toulouse, officers used water cannon against an unauthorised demonstration attended by several thousand people, mostly young protesters.Student groups said they planned further high school and university blockades on Tuesday and Thursday, before joining a demonstration called by workers and trade unions on November 5.In Germany, police used water cannon to disperse crowds after youth-led demonstrations organised by the group “Gen Z regelt!” turned violent in several cities. The rallies, held under the slogan of better education, healthcare, climate action and affordable living, had largely remained peaceful before clashes broke out towards the evening.In Frankfurt, at least two stores were looted and several others damaged, while police struggled to regain control, according to a Reuters witness. In Cologne, officers used water cannon after protesters allegedly targeted them with fireworks. In Berlin, demonstrators threw bottles and eggs, while protesters in Hamburg set barricades on fire, Bild reported.Fresh anti-government protests also took place in Albania’s capital, Tirana, where demonstrators renewed calls for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. A march outside the education ministry turned violent when masked youths threw paving stones and firebombs at police and set rubbish bins alight.Police were also on alert in Barcelona after an anonymous TikTok network called Blocus urged fresh gatherings, and in Italy following recent clashes in Milan, Turin and Bologna.
Article Summary: Four police officers and one gendarme injured in Paris, with three officers suffering burns from Molotov cocktails. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said around 150 planned demonstrations had passed off peacefully. An estimated 320,000 people took part in demonstrations across the country, down from 410,000 the previous weekend.

Article Title: ‘We can do it in 10 minutes’: Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran, names Pickaxe Mountain
Article Text:
Trump escalates pressure on Tehran

Trump, Netanyahu hold telephone conversation

Rubio says diplomatic talks remain active

Amid reports of renewed military consultations between Washington and Israel over possible strikes against Iran, US president Donald Trump said on Saturday that American forces could strike one or two remaining Iranian nuclear sites within 'ten minutes'. He claimed that the US had already 'knocked out' Iran's nuclear capabilities, but said some targets remained to be dealt with.Speaking to reporters at a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida, Trump said the US had yet to deal with one or two targets, specifically referring to the underground facility known as Pickaxe Mountain.“We've knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in ten minutes,” Trump said.Trump specifically pointed to one or two remaining high-priority nuclear targets in Iran, including the fortified underground installation known as Pickaxe Mountain.“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added.Despite the military warning, Trump indicated that Washington remained open to a negotiated settlement with Tehran. He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to develop nuclear weapons.However, he questioned Iran's reliability in the discussions.“Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They want to make a deal; we'll find out about that,” he said.Asked about the progress of negotiations, Trump said, “They're going fine, but they're not very reliable. They make a deal and then they back out.”The US President's remarks came amid escalating rhetoric from Tehran, with Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei warning that any threat from the United States or Israel would invite an immediate response.According to Iran's official IRNA news agency, Khamenei said that “any kind and level of threat” from Washington or Tel Aviv should be met with an immediate response, without geographical limitations.Iranian state media reported that Khamenei made the remarks during a meeting with military chiefs.Khamenei has not appeared publicly since the war began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28. He assumed the position of supreme leader after the initial wave of attacks killed his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with several other senior Iranian officials.Earlier, Trump reportedly spoke with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu by telephone on Saturday morning, as Washington assessed options for potentially resuming military operations against Iran.According to The Wall Street Journal, which cited people familiar with the conversation, the two leaders discussed the situation amid preparations for possible renewed strikes. The call followed a White House meeting earlier in the week at which Trump consulted senior military officials on options for restarting major combat operations, the newspaper reported.However, Washington has not announced any decision to launch fresh attacks.US secretary of state Marco Rubio earlier said diplomatic engagement with Iran had continued, even as the administration considered its military options. Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, Rubio declined to set a deadline for negotiations or assess their progress.“There are multiple talks; talks have actually never stopped. There's been active conversations going both in some cases directly, but often through intermediaries,” Rubio said.He added that Washington remained open to a diplomatic agreement, provided it addressed American security concerns.“I'm not gonna characterise either the progress on those talks or any timeframe on it other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” he said.
Article Summary: Donald Trump says US has 'knocked out' Iran's nuclear capabilities. However, he said some targets remained to be dealt with, including Pickaxe Mountain. Trump indicated that Washington remained open to a negotiated settlement with Tehran. He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to develop nuclear weapons.

Article Title: 2 women killed, several injured as speeding bus runs amok in Bhubaneswar
Article Text:
The rear end of the ill-fated car was completely damaged.





BHUBANESWAR: In a horrific series of road accidents, two women were killed and several others injured after a speeding passenger bus went on a rampage in the Nayapalli area of Bhubaneswar early Sunday morning.The incident occurred near CRP Square when a night coach bus allegedly lost control and ploughed into morning walkers before crashing into vehicles parked along the roadside. The bus first hit pedestrians and then rammed into a parked car and a goods-carrying auto-rickshaw, dragging the vehicles nearly 100 metres. It also crashed into a roadside tea stall and damaged an underground drinking water chamber.The impact was so severe that the rear portion of the car was completely mangled. Two women reportedly died on the spot, while several others sustained injuries. The injured were rushed to Capital Hospital for treatment.The deceased have been identified as Geetanjali Rana (24), a resident of Bargarh district, and Juna Mandal (41), a resident of Nayagarh. The injured include Pradeep Jena (45) and Sunita Meher (26).The bus driver allegedly fled the scene immediately after the accident, triggering a search for the vehicle and its driver.Nayapalli police rushed to the spot, dispersed the crowd and initiated an investigation. Police are examining the circumstances leading to the accident to establish the sequence of events and identify the absconding driver.The tragic incident has once again raised serious concerns over reckless driving, overspeeding and pedestrian safety on the roads of the capital city.
Article Summary: Two women killed and several others injured in Bhubaneswar. Bus allegedly lost control and ploughed into morning walkers before crashing into vehicles parked along the roadside. Bus driver allegedly fled the scene immediately after the accident, triggering a search for the vehicle and its driver.

Article Title: ‘Your father is waiting’: How 8-year-old lured KG girl into empty classroom before brutal attack in Panchkula; staff remained unaware until parents arrive
Article Text:
An eight-year-old boy lured a six-year-old girl into a classroom and assaulted her at a school.

Teacher handling two classes with around 80 students

Attack raises concerns over aggression among children





PANCHKULA: An eight-year-old boy lured a six-year-old kindergarten girl into an empty classroom at a government school in Panchkula on October 28, telling her that her father was waiting there, before launching a brutal assault on her, CCTV footage shows.The boy allegedly kicked and punched the girl and banged her head against desks. The assault continued even after she lost consciousness, according to the footage.The circumstances that led to the attack remain unclear, and police are investigating the possible motive.The incident went unnoticed by school staff. It was only after the girl's parents learnt that she was missing from her usual pickup point that they rushed to the school and began searching for her. The girl was eventually found injured inside the premises.The disturbing CCTV footage has since circulated on social media, raising questions about the supervision of young children and the school's response to the incident.The girl is undergoing treatment at PGI-Chandigarh and is reported to be stable. Police have registered an FIR against the school principal and the class teacher.The eight-year-old boy was presented before the Juvenile Justice Board for psychological evaluation.A brain mapping test was conducted at PGI-Chandigarh on Saturday, with another round scheduled for Monday, sources said.Police are also examining whether exposure to online games or television content could have influenced the boy's behaviour. No trigger for the assault has been established so far.A departmental inquiry into the incident has pointed to possible lapses in student supervision, with statements suggesting that a shortage of teachers had led to two classes being conducted together.According to sources, around 80 students from the two classes were being taught under the supervision of a single teacher.The class teacher told the inquiry committee that she was handling both classes on the day of the incident. She said the school had closed classes at around 3.15pm and that she had led the children in a line through a corridor towards the kitchen area as parents began arriving to collect them.The teacher later returned to the staff room, while a school attendant monitored the handover of children to their parents.Around 3.30pm, the autorickshaw driver who regularly ferried the girl informed her father that she was missing from the pickup point. Her family rushed to the school, triggering a search of the premises.The inquiry examined CCTV footage, statements from the boy and accounts given by parents and school employees.The Haryana State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has sought a detailed factual report, supporting documents and an action-taken report from the district education officer. The preliminary inquiry has been completed, and its findings are to be forwarded to the education directorate for consideration of further action over the alleged lapses.DCP Aditya Singh said mandatory standard operating procedures would be issued for schools, alongside sensitisation and outreach programmes.The assault has prompted child psychologists and paediatricians to call for early intervention to address aggression among young children, with experts stressing the need to examine the circumstances surrounding the behaviour rather than assume a cause.Dr Adarsh Kohli, a clinical psychologist and former professor in PGI's department of psychiatry, said the boy's motives and psychological state needed to be examined. He also stressed the importance of extensive trauma counselling for the girl to address the risk of post-traumatic stress disorder and long-term difficulties with trust.Dr Bhavneet Bharti, a social paediatrician at PGI who works on adverse childhood experiences and the impact of social media on children, said an eight-year-old was still developing emotional regulation, impulse control and the ability to manage anger and frustration.She said an incident of such severity should not be dismissed as ordinary childhood fighting. Investigators and specialists needed to examine whether the child had experienced or witnessed violence, bullying, harsh punishment, emotional distress or other adverse childhood experiences.Bharti called on schools to introduce social-emotional learning from the primary years, helping children recognise anger, tolerate frustration, resolve conflicts and seek help before emotions escalate into aggression.Experts also highlighted the importance of examining children's exposure to violent media, unsupervised screen time and domestic conflict, while avoiding assumptions about what caused the attack.The incident has brought renewed attention to the need for closer supervision in schools, early identification of behavioural concerns and psychological support for children affected by violence.
Article Summary: Teacher handling two classes with around 80 students is accused of lapses in supervision. Child psychologists and paediatricians call for early intervention to address aggression among young children. The girl is undergoing treatment at PGI-Chandigarh and is reported to be stable.

Article Title: Heli crash: Did chopper take off during orange alert despite aviation authority’s warning?
Article Text:
Aircraft accident investigation bureau team reaches Uttarkashi to probe chopper crash

Poll Vote & Share your view What action should the UCADA take after the investigation? Strict penalties on the defying party Review and update safety regulations Ensure transparency in the investigation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





DEHRADUN: A day after the helicopter crash near Badrinath claimed the lives of the pilot and five pilgrims from Karnataka, questions were raised on how the chopper was allowed to take off when there was already an orange alert for bad weather, especially since the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) on Saturday said that its orders to halt all flight operations in the area about an hour before the accident were “defied by the heli firm”.UCADA additional chief executive officer (CEO) Sanjay Tolia told TOI that the order was issued by the body’s head of operations, Group Captain Amit Sharma (retd). “UCADA always operates under the rules and regulations of the director general of civil aviation (DGCA) in helicopter operations. On Friday, too, while following the relevant regulations for bad weather, an order was given to halt all flight operations on the Char Dham route, about an hour before the crash. Despite that order, the flight was operated by Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt Ltd,” Tolia said.He added that a probe is on to find the lapses as per DGCA rules and regulations. “It will also find out why the order was defied. A team of Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and DGCA officials have already reached Uttarakhand to initiate their investigation at the crash site. Further action could be taken as per probe findings,” added Tolia.When contacted on the UCADA’s claims, S Bhattacharya, director, flight operations of Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt Ltd, told TOI that he was “based in Delhi, and unaware of any such order”. “An investigation is already on in the whole incident and UCADA will be able to speak on it,” said Bhattacharya.Meanwhile, search and rescue teams comprising personnel from Army, ITBP, SDRF and NDRF resumed their operation on Saturday morning to retrieve the bodies. “The team managed to reach the spot after trekking around 8km across the difficult terrain through Pandukeshwar,” said Chamoli DM Gaurav Kumar.“The mortal remains would be taken to Govindgarh and onwards to Dehradun where authorities would hand them to their families after completing the required procedure,” the DM added.
Article Summary: The Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) said that its orders to halt all flight operations in the area about an hour before the accident were “defied by the heli firm” Search and rescue teams comprising personnel from Army, ITBP, SDRF and NDRF resumed their operation on Saturday.

Article Title: A friend's girlfriend, a rape allegation, a midnight kidnapping: How Bengaluru techie became target of a revenge plot
Article Text:
Manjunath's friend Mahendra





BENGALURU: City police have arrested 11 people, including a 21-year-old woman, for allegedly kidnapping a 23-year-old techie and his housemate and demanding a ransom of Rs 10 lakh. The techie, rescued along with his friend from a rented house in Nagarabhavi Wednesday afternoon, has also been arrested after the woman accused him of rape.The techie, Bursu Mahendra alias B Mahendra, a native of Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh, lived in Munnekolalu. Police said the woman’s rape complaint emerged during the investigation into the kidnapping, leading to a separate criminal case against Mahendra.According to investigators, Mahendra was a close friend of Marripati Manjunath alias Manja, who also lived in Munnekolalu. Mahendra was acquainted with Galeti Rajkumar alias Raj, 24, as well.Police said Raj had brought his girlfriend to Manjunath’s house on the night of Oct 24, when Manjunath was away. Mahendra and his housemate Tarun allegedly entered the house around midnight and found Raj with the woman. According to an investigating officer, the two men allegedly assaulted the woman sexually, with Tarun locking Raj in a room while Mahendra allegedly raped her in another room.The two men fled after Manjunath returned home, police said.Deciding to teach the two men a lesson, Rajkumar along with Manjunath mobilised others to kidnap Mahendra and Tarun. Police said the group barged into Mahendra’s house around 2am Wednesday and abducted both men. They allegedly confined them in a room at a rented house in Nagarabhavi before Rajkumar called Mahendra’s father, Ramana, and demanded Rs 10 lakh for their release.Ramana, who was in Madanapalle, was allegedly told to bring the money and wait near Hoskote bus stand. He rushed to Bengaluru and approached Marathahalli police, who launched a probe.Whitefield DCP Saidulu Adavat said special teams were formed to trace the suspects and rescue the hostages. “Using digital clues and information from locals, our teams traced the hideout, rescued the two men, and arrested the accused,” he said.The 11 arrested for kidnapping are Rajkumar, Manjunath, Loknath, Suhail, Narendra Reddy, Shiva Subramanyam, Saleem Pasha, Nayeem Pasha, Shabaz, Rajesh, and the woman.A senior police officer said investigators learnt about the woman’s rape allegation only after the arrests. Cops are now investigating both the alleged sexual assault and the kidnap-for-ransom case.
Article Summary: Bursu Mahendra, a 23-year-old techie, was rescued along with his friend from a rented house in Nagarabhavi Wednesday afternoon. Police said the woman’s rape complaint emerged during the investigation into the kidnapping, leading to a separate criminal case.

Article Title: SC upholds Telangana’s claim over 550 acres prime land worth Rs 25K crore in Miyapur
Article Text:
The Hyderabad Metro Rail depot at Miyapur is also part of the land parcel.





HYDERABAD: In a big win for Telangana govt in a 23-year-old legal battle, Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a batch of appeals filed by private individuals claiming over 550 acres of prime land at Miyapur, upholding the then AP high court’s finding and the decision of the special court for land grabbing cases that the land belongs to the state.According to sources, the land parcel (in survey numbers 100 & 101) in Miyapur abuts the National Highway-65. Incidentally, the Hyderabad Metro Rail depot at Miyapur is part of the land parcel, valued at over Rs 25,000 crore.“We find no perversity in the findings recorded by both the special court and the high court on this aspect,” a Supreme Court bench, comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, said.The court said it saw no reason to invoke equity, describing the matter as "a clear-cut case of attempts being made to grab valuable land vested in the state”. Since the appellants’ own title was lacking, "there was no question of granting equitable relief”, the bench held.Writing the judgments for the bench, Justice Sundresh noted that the land parcels were classified as 'sarkari poramboke’ after the 1912 survey.Miyapur later formed part of a Paigah jagir restored to one Rafi-un-nisa Begum on the recommendation of the Justice Reilly Commission (which inquired into the settlement of Paigah estates) and confirmed by the 1929 ‘firman (farman)’ by the Nizam.The court, however, held that a jagir was a grant of rights in respect of land revenue, not of title, and that the firman itself restricted sale, mortgage or gift without the Nizam’s sanction.Whatever limited rights existed were extinguished by the AP (Telangana Area) (Abolition of Jagirs) Regulation, in force from Aug 15, 1949, under which jagirs were included in the ‘Diwani’ and the jagirdars’ powers and rights had ceased.The court explained that a jagirdar’s entitlement after abolition was confined to the commutation sum, a one-time payment in the nature of compensation. It added that the exceptions for home farms and personal property under Regulations 17 and 18 apply only if proved, and the burden lies on the person asserting them.The judges found the revenue entries pertaining to the land naming Rafi-un-nisa Begum as pattadar in the 1950s pahanies "bogus and not genuine”, the product of fraud in collusion with revenue officials.They further refused to consider a plea raised by the appellants, for the first time in Supreme Court, that the land was bought at an auction in 1918 and bequeathed to Rafi-un-nisa Begum by will in 1943-44.It said the documents had not passed the tests of admissibility, relevancy and proof, were never mentioned in the Reilly Commission (which inquired into the settlement of Paigah estates and the inter se claims) report or any earlier proceeding, and contradicted a century of public state records. The apex court also found that adverse possession was neither proved nor available.Even assuming the land was settled on their predecessor under the 1929 firman, the court said, it conveyed no title and any interest was extinguished by the Abolition Regulation.As Rafi-un-nisa Begum herself lacked a valid title, she could not have passed it to the appellants. The plea that the land was “Zat Jagir” (personally granted property) was rightly rejected, as it was never raised before the special court and no evidence was led on it.The court further noted that some appellants before it were not parties before the special court or high court.The bench also took note of transfer of some of the land parcels to the Hyderabad Urban Development Authority (now HMDA) , but declined to go into the inter se disputes among the claimants.Reacting to the development, the chief minister’s office (CMO) in an official release stated: “A special initiative by chief minister A Revanth Reddy led to the resolution of the Miyapur case pending for 23 years.” The CM directed officials to expedite legal proceedings to protect these highly valuable govt land parcels, it added.BOXGovt records from 1912 listed the land as state property. In the 1920s, the Nizam restored the village to the Paigah family, but only with limited rights. When the Nizam’s old estates were abolished in 1949, the land passed to the state, and the Paigah heirs accepted compensation. Decades later, other claimants surfaced, relying on revenue entries in another heir’s name. In 1997, the special court for land-grabbing cases ruled the land belonged to the state. In 2003, the then Andhra Pradesh high court upheld this, declaring the claimants land grabbers. The private parties challenged high court’s verdict by moving the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a batch of appeals filed by private individuals claiming over 550 acres of prime land at Miyapur. The court said it saw no reason to invoke equity, describing the matter as "a clear-cut case of attempts being made to grab valuable land vested in the state"

Article Title: Jamia set to hold student body polls after 22 years; 18-day hunger strike ends
Article Text:
Students celebrate after their demands are accepted

Polls at Jamia likely in Aug next year, 18-day hunger strike ends





NEW DELHI: After over two decades without an elected students' union, Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is set to return to campus democracy, with the university committing to complete the union constitution by May 15, 2027, and hold elections by Aug 27, 2027. The last union election was held in 2005, reports Sugandha Jha.The breakthrough came late Thursday after registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi visited the protest site around 9pm and held talks with the agitating students, bringing the 18-day hunger strike to an end on the university's 106th Foundation Day. The registrar's order, issued after the discussions, addressed the protesters' central demand for a time-bound roadmap to restore elected student representation. It also directed the withdrawal of disciplinary action linked to the stir.The five hunger strikers ended their fast with juice offered by the registrar. Celebrations broke out at the protest site after the order to complete union polls and constitution was issued.The order stated: “The approval and implementation of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union Constitution shall be completed by May 15, 2027.Subsequent to the approval of the Constitution, the university shall release the notification for elections in accordance with the recommendations and guidelines of the Lyngdoh Committee. This date will be in accordance with the guidelines set forth by the Lyngdoh Committee regulations. The elections shall be conducted within six weeks of the start of the academic session, i.e., approximately within six weeks from July 16, 2027.”On disciplinary proceedings, the administration directed: “All ongoing show-causes notices, disciplinary actions, rustications, suspensions and campus ban orders issued in connection with participation in the protest period shall be revoked.”“In view of the above, the protesting students shall call off their hunger strike with immediate effect,” it added.The resolution came on a day when JMI’s customary Foundation Day celebrations were curtailed amid the agitation. Instead of the usual programme, the official observance was limited to flag hoisting and the university anthem, while protesting students organised an ‘Inquilabi Mela’ at Gulistan-e-Ghalib near Gate No. 7. Hunger strikers Ebin Basil and Rehan Khan were designated ‘chief guests’ at the parallel event, which featured speeches and the release of a protest report and memorandum.Jamia traditionally marks its foundation day with weeklong celebrations attended by prominent dignitaries. Last year, Union minister Kiren Rijiju was the chief guest. This year, the agitation overshadowed the occasion, turning it into a platform for students to press for democratic representation.How the standoff escalatedThe agitation began on Oct 12, with students demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU), which has remained defunct since 2006. On Oct 24, the administration issued an order accepting the protesters’ demands and stating elections would be held within 15 days of approval of the students’ union constitution after the agitation grew bigger and gained support from political figures. However, the order did not specify a deadline for completing the constitution, leaving a key procedural step open-ended and failing to address the protesters’ demand for a time-bound roadmap.The movement intensified as five students — Ebin Basil, Rehan Khan, Ritik, Altaf and Abuzar — began an indefinite hunger strike. Their demands also included the release of students in police custody and Tihar Jail, withdrawal of show-cause notices issued to female students, and removal of the chief proctor and security adviser.The standoff subsequently saw clashes between students and security personnel, increased security deployment, restrictions on campus gatherings and a shift to online classes. Protesters also faced disciplinary proceedings, campus-ban orders and directions for some students to leave the campus. The university is now expected to resume physical classes soon.
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is set to return to campus democracy. University to complete union constitution by May 15, 2027, and hold elections by Aug 27. Last union election was held in 2005. 18-day hunger strike ends on university's 106th Foundation Day.

Article Title: 3 siblings found dead in flat near Mumbai; trio recorded video before tragedy
Article Text:
Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.





VIRAR: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday, with police suspecting they died by suicide after consuming poison.In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties, police said.The deceased were identified as Kumar Mehta (50), Dipesh Mehta (52) and Khevana Mehta (48). They lived in flat No. 1203 in the D wing of Garden Avenue in Global City. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.Bolinj police reached the spot and broke open the door around 2.30am on Thursday. The bodies were found in a decomposed state inside the flat.According to police, the siblings had been living in the rented flat since 2025. One of them had suffered paralysis, while one of the brothers was undergoing treatment for cancer.In the video recorded in Gujarati before their deaths, they reportedly spoke about their health problems and financial distress.Senior inspector Prakash Kawale of Bolinj police station said the siblings may have died three to four days before their bodies were discovered. Their bodies have been sent for postmortem examination.Police also contacted the siblings’ sister, who told investigators that the three were facing financial difficulties and had sought money from her as well.
Article Summary: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat. Police suspect they died by suicide after consuming poison. In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties.

Article Title: TVK leader Christopher arrested for sexually harassing college student after offering lift
Article Text:
TVK leader Christopher





KANYAKUMARI: A functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a college student after offering her a lift home in Tamil Nadu’s Kanyakumari district, police said.Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him. He hails from Marundhukottai near Thuckalay.The complainant, a second-year college student from Kulasekaram, studies at a private college in Nagercoil. She regularly travelled with another student from Moolachal, who is also a TVK member, police sources said.On the day of the incident, the two students were waiting for a bus after college when it began raining. Christopher, who knew the other student, stopped his car and offered to drop them home, saying he was travelling in the same direction.After dropping the other student at Moolachal, Christopher continued towards Kulasekaram with the complainant, assuring her that he would drop her near her home, police said.The student alleged that Christopher stopped the vehicle along the way and sexually harassed her. She confronted him and tried to get out of the car to escape, according to police sources. He later dropped her near her residence and fled.The student informed her parents after reaching home and subsequently told her college friend about the incident. The two then approached Thuckalay police station and lodged a complaint.Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) functionary arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a college student. Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him.

Article Title: Ex-Congress worker shot at, dragged out of car, attacked with sharp weapons in Ludhiana
Article Text:
The accused allegedly fired five to six rounds, following, Jagjot suffered splinter injury near his eye.





LUDHIANA: A group of assailants allegedly fired multiple shots at a property dealer and former Congress worker in Dholewal late Wednesday night when he was with his mother and three-year-old son.The victim, Jagjot Singh, sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon and fled.Singh, a resident of Miller Gunj, managed to drive away with his mother and son despite the attack and reach Civil Hospital, where he received treatment.Singh said the family had ordered food while sitting in the car. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him.He rushed back into the car, but the accused allegedly tried to pull him out and attacked him with sharp-edged weapons. As he resisted and attempted to drive away, they fired several rounds at the car, shattering its windowpanes.Singh alleged that he knew the attackers and claimed the same people had attacked his house and opened fire about a year ago over a rivalry.He also alleged a political angle, saying he was previously associated with the Congress but was no longer affiliated with any political party.He claimed the attackers belonged to another political party and held a grudge against him over electoral rivalry.ACP (Industrial Area-B) Anubhav Jain said police had identified the accused, who allegedly had a rivalry with Singh over their previous political associations. The main accused was identified as Jaswinder Singh, who was accompanied by his aides. An FIR has been registered.
Article Summary: Jagjot Singh, a property dealer and former Congress worker, was with his mother and three-year-old son. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him. He sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon.

Article Title: 6 dead in MP: 2 sisters, one 8 months pregnant, and 4 children found in separate wells
Article Text:
Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday.





BHOPAL: Two sisters, one of whom was eight months pregnant, allegedly jumped into wells with their four children in two separate incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Shivpuri district on Wednesday, leaving all six dead.Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, Sita Rawat, 40, was found dead with her three children — Rakhi, 14, Priyanka, 11, and Shlok, 6 — in a well in Khonkar village, under Kolaras police station limits.Police are investigating the two incidents separately and are yet to establish the reasons behind the deaths.Anjali’s three daughters were also present when she allegedly jumped into the well with her son. Her eldest daughter, Monika, rescued herself and her two younger sisters before returning home and informing family members. Relatives rushed to the spot and pulled Anjali and Prashant out of the well, but both had died. Anjali’s unborn child also died.According to family members, Anjali’s husband, Dharmveer Singh Rawat, died in a road accident around one-and-a-half months ago.Police are examining the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sita, a resident of Sesai village, had gone to a field in Khonkar village with her three children. When they had not returned home by around 6pm, relatives began searching for them.They found slippers near a well and spotted a child’s body inside, following which they alerted the police. Kolaras police retrieved the bodies of Sita and her three children by around 11pm.Family members said the sisters were close and frequently spoke to each other over the phone. They suspect Sita may have been affected by Anjali’s death earlier that day, but police have not established any link between the two incidents.Postmortem examinations of all six deceased were scheduled for Thursday. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding both incidents.
Article Summary: Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday. Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, SitaRawat, 40, was found dead with her three children in a well in Khonkar village. Police are investigating the two incidents separately.

Article Title: How dispute over hotel lease escalated into mass shooting at Guwahati's Bilas Inn, with leaseholder killing 4 linked to owner's family
Article Text:
A deadly shooting occurred at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati, leaving five people dead and one injured.

Accused arrested, licensed pistol seized

Congress raises law and order concerns

GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Police apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting.A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. His condition was stable, a senior doctor said.A forensic and scientific investigation is underway, with specialised teams examining the crime scene and collecting evidence. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. He called on chief minister and home minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to take responsibility and pay greater attention to rising crime.Gogoi, the deputy leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, also called for a thorough inquiry, accountability and concrete measures to prevent similar incidents.
Article Summary: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night. The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker. The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, was arrested within an hour of the incident.

Teerath Singh (L) was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village while his friend sustained injuries (R: File photo used for representation)

AMRITSAR: The son of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch was shot dead and his friend was injured when assailants opened fire on them outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village, falling under Chatiwind police station, on Monday evening.The victim, Teerath Singh, was returning after paying obeisance at the gurdwara along with his friend Ranjit Singh when the assailants allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving both injured.Teerath was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead, officials said.Yadwinder Singh, Deputy superintendent of police (DSP), Attari, said that Ranjit, who sustained a bullet injury, is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.The preliminary investigations suggested that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.He further said police have identified four persons, Gurditt Singh, Gurjant Singh, Harkirat Singh alias Hockey, and Gora, and registered an FIR naming them, but no arrests have been made so far.The DSP said that teams have been constituted to investigate the case and arrest the accused.Police sources also informed that the family of Teerath also suspects the involvement of a rival group from the village behind the incident.Notably, Teerath’s brother Karaj Singh had won the sarpanch election on an AAP ticket.The killing triggered a political attack on the AAP government, with former union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu questioning its ability to maintain law and order in Punjab.In a X post, he said, “The murder of Teerath Singh, brother of an incumbent AAP sarpanch, outside a gurdwara in Amritsar is a stark indictment of Punjab’s collapsed law and order. Article Title: Iran declares UK navy, air force 'terrorist' groups, puts MI6 in hostile list
Article Text:
The Iranian foreign ministry accused Britain of supporting military operations against Tehran, particularly by facilitating access to bases

Iran has designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist organisations" and classified its foreign intelligence agency, MI6, as a "hostile group", in a retaliatory move that marks a fresh escalation in tensions between Tehran and London.The decision brings Britain's military and intelligence establishments under the scanner of Iranian security laws amid the ongoing confrontation over the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.According to news agency ANI, Iran's foreign ministry announced the measures on Sunday, accusing Britain of supporting military operations against Tehran by providing access to its bases and logistical facilities.The ministry also cited Britain's July decision to bring Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under its State Threats Act 2026, describing the move as part of London's hostile actions against the Islamic Republic.In its statement, Iran's foreign ministry described Britain's actions against Tehran as "hostile and unlawful", accusing London of violating the principles of the United Nations Charter and international law.The ministry said the decision was a response to Britain's actions over the past year, including its alleged involvement in the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran through the provision of military bases, facilities and logistical support.Defending the latest measures, the ministry said they had been adopted "in accordance with the principles of international law and within the framework of the principle of reciprocity". It further warned that "the British government will bear responsibility for the consequences of this action", holding London accountable for the fallout from the decision.The latest development is significant as Iran has extended its retaliatory action beyond Britain's conventional armed forces to its foreign intelligence establishment, classifying MI6 as a "hostile group".MI6, formally known as the Secret Intelligence Service (SIS), is Britain's foreign intelligence agency responsible for gathering intelligence overseas and identifying threats to the country's national security.It operates outside the UK, collecting information on foreign governments, terrorist networks, espionage activities and other potential security threats, and provides intelligence to the British government.
Article Summary: Iran has designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist organisations" It has also classified its foreign intelligence agency, MI6, as a "hostile group" The decision brings Britain's military and intelligence establishments under the scanner of Iranian security laws.

Article Title: Lucknow murder caught on cam: Friend stabs youth to death 3 days after his release from Agra jail; viral video sparks hunt for accused
Article Text:
Youth stabs to death a man in Saadatganj area of Lucknow and flees





LUCKNOW: A 24-year-old man was allegedly stabbed to death by his acquaintance following a heated argument near Ambedkar Park in Lucknow's Saadatganj area on Saturday evening.The incident gained widespread attention after a video purportedly showing the aftermath of the attack and the accused fleeing the scene went viral on social media.The victim, identified as Rehan, a resident of Ramnagar, suffered multiple stab wounds, including a deep injury to his neck. He was rushed to the trauma centre of King George's Medical University (KGMU), where doctors declared him dead during treatment.Police said Rehan had gone for a walk with his acquaintance, Uzaifa, a resident of Gulab Ki Bagiya. The two were near Ambedkar Park in Azad Nagar's C Block when an argument broke out.Investigators are yet to ascertain what triggered the dispute. During the altercation, Uzaifa allegedly pulled out a knife and repeatedly attacked Rehan before fleeing.A video that surfaced online shortly after the incident allegedly captures the moments following the stabbing and shows the accused running away from the spot. Police are examining the footage, which is expected to form a key part of the investigation.The murder has shocked the victim's family, as Rehan had returned home only three days earlier after being released from Agra jail. His wife, Seeba, said he had left home around 6 pm on Saturday and the family was later informed about the attack.Rehan's father, Munshi, said his son had spent nearly one-and-a-half months in jail and had been released only a few days earlier. He claimed Rehan had been falsely implicated in the case.Senior police officers, including DCP (West) Jitendra Srivastava and ACP Ranjit Kumar, visited the crime scene and reviewed the evidence. Police have initiated inquest proceedings and are awaiting the post-mortem report.A murder case is being registered based on the family's complaint, while multiple teams have been deployed to trace the absconding accused. Investigators are probing both the motive behind the dispute and the sequence of events leading to the fatal stabbing.
Article Summary: A 24-year-old man was allegedly stabbed to death by his acquaintance following a heated argument in Lucknow's Saadatganj area. The victim, identified as Rehan, suffered multiple stab wounds, including a deep injury to his neck. A video purportedly showing the aftermath of the attack and the accused fleeing the scene went viral on social media.

Article Title: A former Air Force officer claims wife accused him of extra-marital affairs and alcoholism without evidence. Now after 12 years, Mumbai court grants divorce, says unsubstantiated allegations about spo
Article Text:
(Representative image) A Family Court in Mumbai ruled that unsubstantiated allegations of character and behavior can constitute mental cruelty.





MUMBAI: Making unsubstantiated allegations about a spouse's character, extra-marital affairs and drinking habits amounts to mental cruelty and can be grounds for divorce, a Family Court has ruled while dissolving the marriage of a 59-year-old former Air Force officer. The verdict ends a legal battle spanning 12 years, six months and 19 days.The court allowed the husband's counter-claim for divorce on grounds of cruelty, recognised his right to reside in the couple's Kandivli flat and directed his wife to return the original property documents of their Kandivli and Santacruz flats.Observing that cruelty is not defined under the Hindu Marriage Act, the judge said it is a relative term that varies from person to person and depends on the spouses' status and circumstances. Serious allegations about a spouse's character without corroborative evidence could cause mental cruelty, the court held.The husband's advocate, Kanupriya Kejriwal, argued that his wife had made reckless allegations of extra-marital affairs and alcoholism without supporting evidence. She also pointed out that the husband's testimony remained unchallenged as the wife had not cross-examined him. The couple married in Dec 1997 in Mumbai and have a daughter, who was a teenager when the legal battle began.The wife, a practising lawyer, filed for divorce and sought relief under the Domestic Violence Act in early 2014, alleging physical, sexual, psychological and economic abuse. She also accused her husband of being violent, alcoholic and unfaithful.The husband denied the allegations, claiming his wife repeatedly suspected him of having affairs during official trips, insulted him and created a hostile atmosphere at home. He also alleged that she pressured him to leave the Indian Air Force for a private-sector job and later lodged a false police complaint.The court noted that the wife's father admitted that allegations of extra-marital affairs were based on information received from her, not personal knowledge. It treated the evidence as largely hearsay.
Article Summary: A Family Court in Mumbai ruled that unsubstantiated allegations of character and behavior can constitute mental cruelty. The verdict ends a legal battle spanning 12 years, six months and 19 days. The husband's advocate argued that his wife had made reckless allegations of extra-marital affairs and alcoholism.

Article Title: ‘I’ll frame you in a women’s case’: Digital media COO, Juhi Mehta, arrested for ‘driving BMW at Mumbai traffic cop’, gets bail later
Article Text:
Juhi Mehta, the COO of a digital media company, collided her BMW with another vehicle in Vile Parle West

Video captures confrontation

Hatchback driver alleges rear-end collision





MUMBAI: A digital media company's chief operating officer (COO), Juhi Mehta, allegedly threatened to frame a traffic constable in a case involving a crime against women and then drove her BMW towards him after he asked her to move the car following a collision in Vile Parle West on Friday evening.Juhu police arrested her on Saturday, and she was released on bail later that day.According to the FIR, constable Prashant Hake, 36, attached to the Santacruz traffic division, was on duty at Mahabharti Junction, opposite Pratiksha bungalow, when he noticed a crowd gathering between 8.15pm and 8.30pm. On reaching the spot, he found that a BMW driven by Mehta and a hatchback had collided, leaving both vehicles obstructing traffic.Hake asked the two motorists to move their vehicles to one side to clear the road. However, according to his statement, Mehta allegedly refused to comply and attempted to leave the spot.When Hake stood in front of her BMW and repeated his instructions, Mehta allegedly argued with him and threatened to frame him in a case involving a crime against women.According to Hake's statement, Mehta began driving despite seeing him standing in front of the car.The constable then signalled to a bystander to record the incident.The video shows the uniformed policeman repeatedly asking Mehta to wait until other police personnel arrived, while she presses the accelerator. The bystander recording the incident also knocked on the car's window and asked her to stop, but she allegedly continued driving. Mehta also began filming the confrontation.Hake told police that he feared being run over and eventually moved out of the car's path. Mehta then allegedly sped away towards JVPD Junction.After Mehta left, Hake spoke to the other motorist, Navinkumar Jha, who was driving the hatchback. Jha told the constable that the BMW had rammed into his vehicle from behind, damaging its taillight, bumper and boot.Hake subsequently approached Juhu police station on Saturday and lodged a complaint. Police registered an FIR under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to intimidation, acts endangering life or personal safety, and the use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging his duty.Police traced Mehta using the BMW's registration number and arrested her on Saturday. She was released on bail later that day.Mehta could not be reached for comment.
Article Summary: Juhi Mehta, the COO of a digital media company, collided her BMW with another vehicle in Vile Parle West on Friday evening. Police constable Prashant Hake, 36, asked her to move the car following the collision. He said she refused and threatened to frame him in a case involving a crime against women. She was arrested on Saturday and released on bail.

Article Title: FDA show-cause notice on ad is pre-judging, punitive: Actor Ajay Devgn
Article Text:
The immediate ceasing action and ‘final warning’ issued indicate FDA has formed a view against him, the actor claimed

Mumbai:





Actor Ajay Devgn has claimed that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in Maharashtra acted with a “premeditated and predetermined mind’’ and with a “prejudged and punitive outlook’’ in issuing him a show-cause notice (SCN) over his appearance in an elaichi (cardamom) commercial. The FDA notices were also issued on Aug 11 by FDA to two other actors who, too, endorsed the flavoured mouth freshener.FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said the actors had sent in their replies. Devgn’s petition said he sent his reply on Aug 21 and said he participated in an advertisement for a brand of elaichi and “did not endorse Vimal Pan Masala.”FDA’s notice said the ad promotes the brand which is “mainly associated with Pan Masala” and sought the actors’ immediate discontinuation of endorsement of the Pan Masala brand and to remove the advertisement from their official social media handles and websites.The ‘Drishyam’ star said the show-cause notice is not what it seems, as he was not given the material on which the notice was issued. His petition, which will be heard on Nov 4 before Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna, said that the grounds ought to have been disclosed to him by FDA to enable an effective response.The “SCN, having been issued without making available the very advertisement on which it is founded, thus fails to afford the Petitioner (Devgn) a meaningful opportunity to show cause and is therefore squarely in the teeth of the principles of natural justice,’’ the petition filed through advocates Parag Khandhar and Chandrima Mitra of DSK Legal contended.The immediate ceasing action and ‘final warning’ issued indicate FDA has formed a view against the actor, his petition contended, without giving him a “genuine opportunity’’ to respond. Besides, under the relevant law called the Food Safety Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, a notice ought to have been mandatorily issued to the brand owner and its explanation sought, and failure to do so showed “non application of mind’’ vitiating the SCN.On Sept 21, FDA issued him a notice to appear on Sept 28, but he sought and was granted an adjournment, after which he filed the petition to challenge the show-cause notice, which questions his endorsement allegedly in violation of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
Article Summary: Ajay Devgn has claimed that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in Maharashtra acted with a “premeditated and predetermined mind’’ FDA issued a show-cause notice (SCN) over his appearance in an elaichi (cardamom) commercial. FDA notices were also issued on Aug 11 by FDA to two other actors who, too, endorsed the flavoured mouth freshener.

Article Title: Digital media COO arrested for ‘driving car at traffic cop’, gets bail

She was released on bail the same day. Mehta could not be reached for her comments.
Article Summary: Juhi Mehta, the Chief Operating Officer of a digital media company, was arrested for allegedly intimidating a traffic policeman. Both the vehicles were blocking traffic movement.

Article Title: HC quashes murder case against man, says delayed witness statements recorded with 'mala fide intention'
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court has quashed an FIR and a subsequent sessions court case against a man in a Diwali banner-dispute murder case. Between 30 and 35 people were named as accused in the FIR, which was registered at Bidkin police station in Oct 2025.The high court specifically observed that the statements of two eyewitnesses were recorded after a 30-day delay with “mala fide intention” to falsely implicate the applicant, Akash Ashok Vanjare, by assigning him a more incriminating role.Justice Sushil M. Ghodeswar allowed the criminal application filed by Vanjare and set aside the FIR registered at Bidkin, the chargesheet, and Paithan Sessions Court’s March 28, 2026, order issuing process against him. The order was originally passed on Oct 15 and modified on Oct 28 following a plea for speaking to the minutes.The FIR was registered on Oct 24, 2025, under Sections 103(1), 189(2), 190, and 191(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Sections 45 and 51 were later added in the chargesheet, and the matter is currently pending as a sessions case.According to the prosecution, a dispute over banners escalated into violence on Oct 23, 2025.Rutik Dharme had put up a Diwali greeting banner near Shivaji Maharaj statue on Oct 20. On Oct 22, Rishikesh alias Chiman Jadhav put up his birthday banner in front of it. The complainant alleged that Vanjare and another individual, Waman Sathe, had instructed Jadhav to place the banner there, a claim based on information passed to the complainant by one Kiran Gujar.The following night, a mob of 30 to 35 persons armed with iron rods, pipes, and sticks allegedly attacked the complainant’s group. Tanmay Ganesh Chormare was struck on the head with an iron rod and succumbed to his injuries on Oct 24.Vanjare’s counsel, advocate Sandeep Rajebhosale, argued that his client was neither present at the spot nor part of the assault or unlawful assembly. He further contended that merely asking for a banner to be put up could not amount to the abetment of murder.The state opposed the plea. Additional public prosecutor A. A. A. Khan cited the statements of witnesses Somnath Tupe and Amol Gade, recorded on Nov 20, 2025, which alleged that the applicant had exhorted the assailants to attack members of the Dhangar community. Advocate Rashmi Kulkarni, appearing for the complainant, also relied on these statements alongside Sections 45 and 51 of the BNS.However, the high court noted that these statements were recorded nearly a month after the incident. They were introduced only after the co-accused had been granted anticipatory bail and the applicant had moved a bail application before the sessions court. The bench observed that despite the presence of “so many eyewitnesses” at the scene, the applicant’s alleged role was not established in any earlier accounts.“The minimum role attributed to him, as stated in the FIR, is that of asking Rushikesh alias Chiman Jadhav to fix the banner,” the high court said, concluding that this act could not amount to abetment and did not attract Sections 45 and 51 of the BNS. It held that the investigating officer had recorded the two delayed statements with a mala fide intention to falsely implicate the applicant.Noting that the high court’s inherent powers under Section 482 of the CrPC are to be used sparingly but are vital to prevent the abuse of the judicial process and secure the ends of justice, Justice Ghodeswar held that neither the FIR nor the subsequent statements disclosed a cognisable offence against the applicant.
Article Summary: The Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court has quashed an FIR and a subsequent sessions court case against a man in a Diwali banner-dispute murder case. The high court specifically observed that the statements of two eyewitnesses were recorded after a 30-day delay with “mala fide intention” to falsely implicate the applicant.
